uncertain.text: Penelope poterat, bis denos ſalua per annos,
uncertain.note: the two Latin verse lines are set in a larger italic display type, indented, with white space above and below; transcribed as one paragraph block because they are a quoted couplet (Propertius) and not a title. A reader could equally have made them two heading blocks per §6.

uncertain.text: peu detoile, qu'elle auoit en ſa main (ce qu'ils luy accor
uncertain.note: 'detoile' is printed closed up (the e of 'de' touches the t of 'toile' at 400%; column measurement gives a 3px gap against 17-24px for this line's word spaces), so left as printed per §1. 'toile,qu'elle' is likewise closed up but the comma rule restores the space.

uncertain.text: touſiours le cœur à ſon Vlyſſes, pour fruſtrer ces gẽtils
uncertain.note: 'à ſon' looks closed up at reading size; a column measurement finds a real if thin space there (this line has a space at every one of its nine word junctions), so it is spaced.

uncertain.text: neſe doit rendte ſi liberalede ſon hõneur, qu'elle doit a-
uncertain.note: three things. (1) 'neſe' and 'liberalede' are printed closed up (8-9px against 17-44px word spaces on this line, and visibly touching at 400%), so left as printed per §1; 'hõneur,qu'elle' is closed up too but the comma rule restores that space. (2) 'rendte' is printed with a clear t (vertical stroke with a crossbar, unlike the shouldered r of 'rend' just before it) where the sense wants 'rendre'; transcribed as printed, sic. (3) the mark over the o of 'hõneur' is a straight macron, taken as the tilde per §2.

uncertain.text: de temps eſt obligée la femme, d'attendreſon mari ab-
uncertain.note: 'd'attendreſon' is printed closed up (no gap between the final e and the long s at 400%, against 17-28px word spaces on this line), so left as printed per §1.

uncertain.text: uoir mille fois plꝰ cher que la vie {m}. toutesfois cela char-
uncertain.note: two doubts on this line. (1) 'plꝰ': after 'pl' the print has a small raised 9-shaped sort, transcribed as ꝰ (U+A770, superscript us) per §2; it could also be read as a raised o. (2) the mark between the italic marker m and 'toutesfois' sits high, at x-height rather than on the baseline, with a faint speck below it; transcribed as a period, but it could be a colon or ink.

uncertain.text: ſ'en faut, qu'il luy peuſt obiecter. ne reprocher telle fau-
uncertain.note: the mark after 'obiecter' is a round dot on the baseline with no tail at 300%, so a period; the sense (ne = ni) would suggest a comma, and a worn comma cannot be ruled out.

the letter before the period reads as an open c rather than the barred italic e used elsewhere in this note; 'latione' (collatione, continuing 'col' from the line above) is the reading given, but 'lationc' is what the glyph looks like at 500%. The final sort of the line is read as the æ ligature.
printed with no gap between 'Properce' and 'au' at 400% (unlike the clear space between 'liure' and 'ij.' on the next line), so left closed up; the sense is 'Properce au liure ij.'

the first sort has the descender and right-curving head of the italic long s, not the looped ascender of the italic l seen in 'la gloſe' and 'liure'; transcribed as ſ although the sense is 'l'Odyſſee'.
the key letter is a squat italic k (the printer's alphabet skips j, so g h i k l m n on this page is regular); it can look like 'lz' at reading size.
after the key l and the capital L there are two marks, a comma-like speck and a period; transcribed as a single period.
the first sort is a c carrying a cedilla hook at 900% (the c of 'cog.' on the line above has none), so transcribed ç; the sense wants 'conſ.' (consanguineam).

printed 're' + space + 'lleximus'; the first sort is a shouldered r, not the curl-topped italic t. With 'c. in' ending the previous line the citation is almost certainly the decretal 'Intelleximus', i.e. 'telleximus', so this may be a turned or wrong sort.
printed with the space after the d rather than after the e ('d eadulter.'); the sense is 'de adulter.' Transcribed as printed.
the sort between 'vij.' and 'ij.' has the closed bowl and crossbar of an italic e and no descender, so it is not the q the citation form ('xxvij. q. ij.') would want; transcribed as printed.
the fourth sort of the numeral is read as v; at 450% it can look like a y or j because of a descending flourish. 'xxxv. q. v.' is the form the citation wants.
